meta.title: Beyond the Desert: Stories of Civilizations
meta.description: Temporary exhibition at Biblioteca Sala Borsa, Bologna, in occasion of the 59th Seminar for Arabian Studies.

hero.tag: Temporary Exhibition · 59th Seminar for Arabian Studies
hero.lead: Step into a land where ancient worlds meet cutting-edge science. From vast deserts to thriving civilizations, discover how archaeology is uncovering the past — and helping us understand the climate challenges of our future.

geography.title: Geography
geography.lead: Six decades of Italian archaeological work mapped across the Arabian Peninsula — from Yemeni highlands to the Omani coast.

history.title: Stories of People and Discoveries
history.lead: Three formative periods reshape what we know about Arabia: not a marginal periphery of the Near East, but an active, connected, dynamic territory.

bronze.title: Bronze Age
bronze.body: Pastoralists, merchants, and artisans moved regularly across Arabia — between oases, coastal sites, and inland routes. Mobility was not backwardness but an organizing principle. Funerary architecture from this period, from monumental tombs at Marib's Temple of Awam to the empty cenotaphs at Baraqish for merchants lost on the Incense Road, reveals a sophisticated symbolic order built around memory, lineage, and territory.

iron.title: Iron Age
iron.body: Stable kingdoms emerge — Saba, Qataban, Ma'in — consolidating control over the Incense Road and the resources of the oases. Necropolises become tools of political identity. External influences from the Levant, Mesopotamia, and the Hellenistic and Roman worlds are absorbed and reinterpreted, never dominant.

preIslamic.title: Pre-Islamic to Islamic
preIslamic.body: Funerary practices simplify; an attention to equality before death anticipates the uniform practices of Islam. Climate, oases, and the falaj irrigation systems shape settlement patterns that endure to the present day.

research.title: UniBo Excavations in Arabia
research.lead: A history of research at three key sites investigated by the University of Bologna.

archive3d.title: 3D Archive
archive3d.lead: Rotate, zoom, and place burial structures from Ras al-Hadd and Halban in your own space using augmented reality. Scan QR codes in the exhibition to view in AR.
